html:
Orissa, now spelled Odisha, is the land on India's east coast along the Bay of Bengal. It was the ancient Kalinga. The map shows a kingdom of Orissa in 1000 and from 1279 to 1600, a time when strong Hindu dynasties ruled it and kept it independent of the Delhi sultans.

The Eastern Gangas (Eastern Ganga dynasty). Anantavarman Chodaganga (ruled 1078 to 1147) united the region, made Cuttack his capital, and began the great Jagannath Temple at Puri. The cult of Jagannath, a form of Vishnu, became the heart of Odia identity. Narasimhadeva I beat back Bengal's Muslim rulers and built the Konark Sun Temple around 1250.

The Gajapatis. In 1434 Kapilendra Deva founded the Gajapati (Suryavamsi) dynasty, "lords of elephants". At its height it reached from the Ganges delta to the Kaveri in the south. His successors fought Vijayanagara for the Andhra coast and lost much of it to Krishnadevaraya. Under Prataparudra Deva, the Bengali saint Chaitanya settled at Puri, spreading devotion to Krishna.

The end came fast. Weak kings followed, and in 1568 the Afghan rulers of Bengal conquered Orissa. By 1592 it was part of the Mughal Empire. Later it passed to the Marathas and in 1803 to the British.
